pr_body:
Attempt to grab the icon for a script type from an extension first, before falling back to the theme.

This adds a method to option_button to allow the ScriptCreateDialog to set the max size of an item icon, so that it can set the size from the Editor Theme when reading the icon from extension.

Example from Godot Dart:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/31a12ea5-64ab-46bd-ae89-f66835519f07)

Fixes #98800
pr_comments: @Ivorforce Updated so that theme takes precedence  unless it returns the fallback icon, at which point it will ask the extension.

issue_context.title: ScriptCreateDialog does not look for icons in GDExtensions
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible 4.x+
- Reproducible in master

### System information

Window 10 (affects all)

### Issue description

When creating a GDExtension that adds a script language (such as [Godot Dart](https://github.com/fuzzybinary/godot_dart)) I want to be able to have the icon show in the Create Script dialog.  This is the current result:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/46a562cb-ed55-49eb-98ed-89fdd581e365)

Although the icon appears properly when the script is attached:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ada1b1d-106a-4132-a367-fc2d7f8a2437)

### Steps to reproduce

- Create a ScriptLanguageExtension for Godot
- Add an icon for the script in the `.gdextension` file under `[icons]`.
- Open the `ScriptCreateDialog`
- Note the lack of icon

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A
comments:
From research - 

The reason this happens is because the `ScriptCreateDialog` only references the theme, and (so far as I know) GDExtensions don't currently have a way to add icons to the theme. ([Relevant code](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/1bffd6c73b44b85e5889f54e14b2193940cf5bb1/editor/script_create_dialog.cpp#L132))

The `EditorNode`, on the other hand, asks the extension for the script's icon ([Relevant code](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/1bffd6c73b44b85e5889f54e14b2193940cf5bb1/editor/editor_node.cpp#L4770)).

The easy way forward here is to just make `ScriptCreateDialog` follow a similar approach as `EditorNode`, and look to see if the icon is defined in the Script's extension first.  

The harder way forward is to support GDExtensions adding theme icons probably....

> The harder way forward is to support GDExtensions adding theme icons probably....

Modules can already add icons, so I think it makes sense for GDExtensions. How custom types register their icons normally?

So far as I can tell, certain areas of the code ask extensions if they have an icon for a particular type, which is registered in the `.gdextension` file.

For example, in my `.gdextension` file I have the following:

```
[icons]

DartScript = "res://godot_dart/logo_dart.svg"
DartHotReload = "res://godot_dart/hot_reload.svg"
```

Certain areas of the editor ask the extension system if they define an icon for a type (such as in [`EditorNode`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/9aed9eca40127bcf21ecd71d25fe8809f345d9e3/editor/editor_node.cpp#L4818) , but others (like the `ScriptCreateDialog`) don't, and only ask the Theme.

I think the larger refactor would be for the Theme to handle asking extensions. My PR is the simpler solution to have `ScriptCreateDialog` work more similarly to `EditorNode`.

review_comments: This can be inside the condition.
It may not be easily doable with how the themes are set up, but don't you think a theme's script language icon should trump the extension's icon, if set explicitly?

Yeah that's a good point.

Debugging through the code though, I'd have to check the return of `get_editor_theme_icon` to see if it's the same icon as default fallback.  That's probably fine? I'll see if I can get it to work.
